slides.title: 5 fireplace myths to drop before you light the first fire

slides.myth: A creosote sweeping log replaces a chimney sweep.
slides.fact: Those logs can loosen some buildup, but chimney pros say they're no substitute for a real mechanical sweep and a yearly inspection.

slides.myth: Toss the wrapping paper in the fireplace after presents.
slides.fact: Wrapping paper can catch all at once and burn super hot, causing a flash fire. Bag it or recycle it instead.

slides.myth: The ashes are cold by the next morning.
slides.fact: Coals can stay hot for days. Scoop ashes into a metal can with a lid and set it outside, at least 10 feet from the house.

slides.myth: Wood you cut this fall is ready to burn this winter.
slides.fact: Softwood needs at least 6 months to dry and hardwood about a year. It's ready under 20% moisture, and a cheap meter can check.

slides.myth: Gas fireplaces never need a checkup.
slides.fact: No soot doesn't mean no problems. Vents can get blocked by nests or debris. Chimneys, fireplaces and vents should be inspected every year.
